verdicts.claim: By default SQLite runs a checkpoint after any COMMIT that leaves the WAL at 1000 pages or more (about 4 MB), and again when the last
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'occurs that causes the WAL file to be 1000 pages or more in size'; 'WAL file accumulates about 1000 pages (and is thus about 4MB'; autocheckpoint page: 'threshold of 1000 or SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT'

verdicts.claim: SQLite found and fixed the WAL-reset bug on 2026-03-03. It is likely present in every release from 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) through 3.51.2
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'On 2026-03-03 ... likely present in all version of SQLite from 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) through 3.51.2 (2026-01-09) ... fixed in version 3.51.3 (2026-03-13) ... 3.44.6 and 3.50.7'; news: 3.53.0 (2026-04-09) is a re-release of 3.52.0, 3.52.0 withdrawn

verdicts.claim: SQLite's 3.51.3 release log lists 'PRAGMA wal_checkpoint=NOOP' and SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP among the changes made since 3.51.0 (2025-11-04)
verdicts.evidence: 3_51_3 release log under 'Prior changes from version 3.51.0 (2025-11-04)': 'Add the PRAGMA wal_checkpoint=NOOP; command and the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP argument'

verdicts.claim: Litestream (v0.5.x) ... truncate-page-n (default 121,359 pages, about 500 MB) ... min-checkpoint-page-count (default 1000) ... checkpoint-interval (1 minute); since v0.5.15 PASSIVE first
verdicts.evidence: db.go: DefaultCheckpointInterval = 1 * time.Minute; DefaultMinCheckpointPageN = 1000; DefaultTruncatePageN = 121359; guide: 'v0.5.15 ... Litestream first attempts a PASSIVE checkpoint'

verdicts.claim: Antithesis ... caught the WAL-reset bug in SQLite 3.51.2 on its first run, after 15 minutes. The same workload passed on 3.51.3.
verdicts.evidence: Antithesis: 'SQL 3.51.2 – still buggy'; 'On my first run, Antithesis caught the bug in 15 mins'; '3.51.3 comes back clean'

verdicts.claim: Tailscale checkpoints manually and 'very aggressively' in its control plane and suffered 19 corruptions in six months
verdicts.evidence: Tailscale: 'we faced 19 separate instances of database corruption over six months'; 'by taking manual control of the checkpointing process and running at our own aggressive pace'

verdicts.claim: Moving to SQLite 3.52.0 ... backup monitor flagged 13 databases. 3.52.0 subtly changed rounding in text-to-floating-point conversions
verdicts.evidence: Tailscale: '13 different databases'; 'subtly changed the rounding behaviour for text-to-floating-point conversions. Our canary shards didn't have any timestamps that triggered'

verdicts.claim: Syncthing's checkpoint-starvation report (GitHub issue 10559, opened 2026-02-04 against v2.0.14) was still open on 2026-10-13. ... 11.6 GiB WAL
verdicts.evidence: GitHub API: state=open, created 2026-02-04, v2.0.14; schaurian 2026-09-12: 'Hit this on v2.1.5', '~400 GiB', '27h', 'db-wal 11.6 GiB', 'db 3.0 GiB'; 2026-09-13: 'Retracting the gate theory', 'WAL went 11.6 GiB -> 97 MB'

verdicts.claim: Since SQLite 3.11.0 (2016-02-15) the WAL for one transaction is proportional to the transaction's size; older versions could write the same page
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'As of SQLite version 3.11.0 (2016-02-15), the WAL file for a single transaction should be proportional in size to the transaction itself'

verdicts.claim: Set PRAGMA journal_size_limit (bytes; default -1, no limit) ... SQLITE_DEFAULT_JOURNAL_SIZE_LIMIT sets the default.
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: 'The default journal size limit is -1 (no limit). The SQLITE_DEFAULT_JOURNAL_SIZE_LIMIT preprocessor macro can be used to change'

notes: All verdicts except the Syncthing claim came from the source cache. The Syncthing issue cache entry had no text, so it took one WebFetch plus a GitHub API read. The WebFetch view hid the relevant schaurian comments as spam, but the API returned their full text.
Minor internal inconsistency, not sampled: line 87 dates Phil Eaton's reproducer 2026-08-24, which is the date of the UPDATE note on wal.html. Line 89 dates the article 2026-08-23.
No reviewer-addressed instructions were found in any source read.
